description: Local core schema and graph integrity validation, plus supported draft profile checks. References and evidence content are not fetched or authenticated.
Enables traversal across interconnected graph entities using semantic, strategic, operational, and governance relationships.
Analyzes graph relationships to identify organizational gaps, overlapping initiatives, unsupported objectives, and emerging strategic opportunities.
Reference implementation extracts graph context and recorded review metadata; runtime orchestration and policy enforcement remain external architectural capabilities.
Proposed federation capabilities; no federation service or adapter is implemented by this reference toolkit.
Execute bundled core schema, graph integrity, assertion and declared supported profile checks; emit JSON conformance results. Does not fetch references or authenticate evidence.
Python command-line script for summarizing ODPG graph metadata, node counts, edge counts, node types, edge types, and confidence values.
Python command-line script for discovering ODPG relationship paths from a node, with optional relationship filtering and reverse traversal.
Report topology gaps and objectives without reviewed support separately; explicitly unaccepted and inactive assertions do not establish support.
Extract graph context preserving assertion metadata, with reviewed paths reported separately. Does not authenticate evidence or grant authorization.
Generate an HTML graph explorer after basic integrity checks; run odpg_validate.py separately for core/profile conformance. Browser viewing loads vis-network from jsDelivr.
An agent definition declares relationships to a product and API. These links neither authorize calls nor prove observed execution.
A data product contributes to a measurable business objective and tracks a KPI.
A data product or API is governed by a policy, enabling governance-aware traversal and impact analysis.

ODPG connects strategic relationships, canonical resource references, evidence pointers and accountable decisions. It complements catalogs, lineage systems, agent runtimes and authorization infrastructure.
Optional Value Evidence profile with hypotheses, metrics, baselines, targets, measurements, evidence and human decisions. Schema and semantic validation do not prove business value.

Separate claim origin from review status. Accepted or observed claims require evidence pointers; accepted/rejected/deferred claims name a reviewer and review timestamp. Review metadata is not authentication.
Proposed distinction between agent definitions and agent runs, capabilities, approvals, policy decisions, evaluations and trace references. Graph edges never authorize tool calls.
Proposed references to PROV and OpenLineage records; no runtime model duplication or implemented adapter is claimed.
Shared graph operations and CLI handlers. Keep beside toolkit CLI scripts, with the bundled schema directory alongside scripts.
Loads local schemas and validates assertion metadata and declared Value Evidence semantics. No standalone CLI; invoked through shared toolkit operations. Does not authenticate evidence.
Synthetic profile fixture with continue and defer review decisions; not observed business results.
Synthetic local resources referenced by the aviation Value Evidence graph; preserve their relative location when running the example.
Import graph topology with a canonical schema URL and string version. Unknown source types remain Resource with a validation warning; assertion history is not imported.
Business, industry, or subject domain covered by the graph. Supports language-specific values.
Explanation of why the graph exists and how it should be used. Supports language-specific values.
Keywords used for discovery, filtering, grouping, and search.
Current status of the graph.
Intended visibility of the graph.
Party responsible for the graph.
